question: What was the complete title of the book in which two James Beard Award winners recommended the restaurant where Ali Khan enjoyed a New Mexican staple in his cost-conscious TV show that started in 2015? Write the numbers in plain text if there are some in the title.
ground_truth: Five Hundred Things To Eat Before It's Too Late: and the Very Best Places to Eat Them

history.name: user
history.content: What was the complete title of the book in which two James Beard Award winners recommended the restaurant where Ali Khan enjoyed a New Mexican staple in his cost-conscious TV show that started in 2015? Write the numbers in plain text if there are some in the title.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Task: Find the complete title of the book where two James Beard Award winners recommended the restaurant Ali Khan visited for a New Mexican staple in his 2015 cost-conscious TV show.
Plan:
- Identify Ali Khan’s show from 2015 and relevant New Mexico episode.
- Determine the New Mexican staple and the restaurant.
- Find the two James Beard Award-winning authors who recommended that restaurant and the specific book title.
- Report the complete book title with any numbers written in words.
Agents: WebSurfer (for browsing), Assistant, FileSurfer.
WebSurfer, first confirm the show details and premiere year, then locate New Mexico episode context.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search query used: Ali Khan cost-conscious TV show 2015 Cooking Channel.
Results summary: The show is Cheap Eats (Cooking Channel). Wikipedia indicates it premiered September 22, 2015. Format: Ali Khan finds four budget-friendly meals per city on a roughly thirty-five dollar budget. This matches the cost-conscious description.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Great. Next, find the New Mexico episode where he eats a New Mexican staple and list the restaurants visited. Specifically identify the place tied to the New Mexican staple (e.g., carne adovada, breakfast burrito, green chile cheeseburger).

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search query used: Cheap Eats Albuquerque episode carne adovada Mary & Tito's.
Findings:
- IMDb/Yidio/Rotten Tomatoes entries for Season 1 Episode 3 (Albuquerque) list featured foods: veggie waffle, green chile cheeseburger, designer donut, and carne adovada.
- Yidio’s synopsis explicitly states Ali visits Mary & Tito’s Cafe, a long-standing Albuquerque spot, and tries their carne adovada (a New Mexican staple).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Proceed assuming the New Mexican staple is carne adovada at Mary & Tito’s Cafe. We need the book in which two James Beard Award winners recommended Mary & Tito’s. Likely candidates are Jane and Michael Stern. Please verify whether they recommended Mary & Tito’s and identify the exact book title where that recommendation appears.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Search query used: Mary & Tito’s Cafe Roadfood Jane Michael Stern.
Result: Roadfood.com entry for Mary & Tito’s Cafe shows a review by Jane & Michael Stern. The page indicates their Roadfood series coverage and mentions the Sterns’ works, including various Roadfood editions and another title by them, 500 Things to Eat Before It’s Too Late. This ties Mary & Tito’s to the Sterns’ recommendations.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open the Google Books page for 500 Things to Eat Before It’s Too Late and capture the exact full title displayed. Also note any series information or other Stern titles shown on that page to ensure we report the complete title correctly.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Opened Google Books for the Sterns’ title.
Visible metadata on the page:
- Title: 500 Things to Eat Before It’s Too Late: and the Very Best Places to Eat Them
- Authors: Jane Stern, Michael Stern
- Publisher/Date: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, 2009
- Series: Roadfood
- Related/More by this author includes: Roadfood: The Coast-to-Coast Guide to 800 of the Best Barbecue Joints, Lobster Shacks, Ice Cream Parlors, Highway Diners, and Much, Much More.
The page clearly presents the full “500 Things…” title as above; “Roadfood” appears as the series, and a separate related Stern title is listed with the long Roadfood subtitle.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Given that Google Books shows the series as Roadfood and highlights the long Roadfood title in the related works, it appears the canonical complete title used in the recommendation context is the Roadfood guide. Please confirm the exact Roadfood subtitle wording and also confirm that Jane and Michael Stern are James Beard Award winners.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Confirmed via Amazon/Google Books: The title reads, “Roadfood: The Coast-to-Coast Guide to 800 of the Best Barbecue Joints, Lobster Shacks, Ice Cream Parlors, Highway Diners, and Much, Much More.”
Checked Wikipedia: Jane and Michael Stern are multiple-time James Beard Award winners (journalism/book awards), so they satisfy the two James Beard Award winners criterion.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Per the user’s instruction, I will convert the numeric value in the title to words before finalizing.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Final answer: Roadfood: The Coast-to-Coast Guide to Eight Hundred of the Best Barbecue Joints, Lobster Shacks, Ice Cream Parlors, Highway Diners, and Much, Much More

mistake_reason: Tool output misinterpretation (FM-4.2): At step 8, WebSurfer displayed unambiguous metadata from Google Books showing the Title field as “500 Things to Eat Before It’s Too Late: and the Very Best Places to Eat Them.” However, at step 9, Orchestrator incorrectly treated the ‘Series: Roadfood’ label and a ‘Related books’ item (“Roadfood: The Coast-to-Coast Guide to 800…”) as the complete title of the relevant book. The agent ignored the explicit Title field and derived a different title from adjacent series/related information, leading to the wrong final answer.
